sentences: A constraint language specifies which local relations may appear in its CSP instances.
The recorded question asks which languages have linear non-redundancy.
Non-redundancy concerns how much of an instance remains essential after logically unnecessary constraints are removed.
A characterization could connect algebraic properties of the language with the possibility of compressing constraint systems.

The saved workshop title does not define the size parameter or redundancy criterion, so the intended linear bound must be recovered before it can be equated with a sparsification theorem or a kernel-size guarantee.
